claims.statement: For every ordinary path-star with m>=1 branches of arities r_i in {2,3,4}, at each actual eligible p (x+2<=p, 3p<2alpha+1, 2p<=alpha) using the least strict zero-extended descent x of P=C+zL^q, the stated conditioned product model satisfies E_j D < 2j-N-(j+1)beta_x/C[x], where j=p-2 and beta_x=binom(q,x)-binom(q,x-1)>0. The result retains the current-p selectors and original tag multiplicities as context but asserts no selector-weighted payment.
claims.scope: Universal informal coefficient lemma on the exact ordinary path-star family with actual first strict descent, all three guards, terminal zero extension, and strict current-p selectors/original multiplicities. It does not imply selected MASS or primary payment and has no Lean award.
claims.reason: The derivative-weight identity is exact. Actual descent gives C[x+1]/C[x] < 1-beta_x/C[x]; positive-interval log-concavity makes adjacent ratios nonincreasing, and j>=x propagates the inequality. All substitutions divide only by positive coefficients.

claims.scope: Finite coefficient-model evidence through m=40 with the actual least strict zero-extended parent descent and literal eligibility guards. It neither establishes a universal conditional-to-unconditioned comparison nor a selector-weighted/payment bound.
claims.reason: The copied producer probe and a separate direct-convolution exact-integer implementation both return 4,308 eligible profiles and no upward discrepancy. Each comparison uses exact rational values; the finite horizon remains bounded evidence.
